mentl/b72590d:
The page runs THE FIXPOINT COMPILER ITSELF: ide/mentl-ide.wasm is the
first-light wheel with one derived change (512MB initial memory instead
of the wheel-scale 4GB; the sed+wat2wasm derivation is in the README).
The loop is proto mentl edit: keystroke → compile (a fresh instance per
run — the bump allocator never frees, so instantiation IS the reset) →
project. Diagnostics parse into a clickable panel (click → jump to the
source line; runtime-internal noise from the linked stdlib is counted,
never listed), the emitted WAT ships with fn/line/time stats and a
download, six demo programs show the verbs, effects, the 200k-frame
constant-stack recursion, floats rendering, string-pattern dispatch,
and refined types. The .mn highlighter gives the five verbs and the ??
hole their accents.

serve.py exists because the compiler's memory is SHARED (the threading
substrate) and browsers require cross-origin isolation for shared
wasm memory — it serves the repo root with COOP/COEP so the page can
also fetch lib/runtime/*.mn to link the runtime exactly as
tools/run-micro.sh does.

Verified headlessly end to end: node ide/test-shim.mjs (the page's
exact import surface under V8) compiles fn double(x)=x*2 to a 66-line
module; the RT-linked effects demo compiles with its handler arm
present; a missing-variable program surfaces E_MissingVariable; and
serve.py answers with the isolation headers, the wasm mime, and the
lib sources. Running the compiled program IN the page needs an
in-browser assembler — the named follow-up Hβ.felt.ide-run-in-page.

Run: python3 ide/serve.py  →  http://localhost:7378/ide/
mentl/b73748c:
The m2 effect-row corruption (the raw 0 in a body-accumulated name set)
was union_row's `na ++ nb` emitted as str_concat: match-binder LLocals
carried handle 0, so BConcat's proof read fell to the string default.
str_concat on a flat list mints a 2-byte string whose fresh-zero bytes
read back as a flat list holding element 0 — every confirmed symptom
(the «invalid-effect» renders, the empty escaping rows, the exit-134
ev-scan floor, the layout-dependent 0-vs-1 flips) is that one emission.

$bind_pat_locals_ctor now mints a bound graph handle for each declared
ctor payload ($graph_fresh_ty + $graph_bind) so lower_var_ref's Lock #1
gives the binder's LLocal a live proof; $pty_canon_seq canonicalizes the
named sequence spellings (EfClosed(List), ENamed(String)) to their
structural tags; nested patterns inherit the payload type.

Census: W_ConcatUnproven 23 to 17, the six h=0 sites (union_row x4,
resolve_row x2) all proven; verify 34/34 through the seed; rungs 7/1
unchanged. The exit-134 floor persists — the corruption root is closed,
the empty-row face stands separately (the infer_ctx nesting discipline,
next).

mentl/b7c683c:
driver_take_first walked last+drop_last, returning the LAST count env
entries REVERSED — and its one consumer persisted that reversal into
the .kai cache's exported_entries. The call site already holds
n_before/n_after, so the exports are the order-preserving
slice(entries_after, n_before, n_after); the lying fn deletes.

take_last computed a PREFIX (pop the snoc end until len<=n) — correct
for its one caller (scope-exit truncating the env back to a mark),
wrong in name. Renamed truncate_to(n, lst), config-first per the
Stage Law, with the algorithm named honestly: take(n)'s contract by
end-pops, right when n is near len.

query_head read last(ws): every 3+-word query classified its verb
from the FINAL word — the same word query_last hands over as the
argument — breaking the documented <verb> [arg] grammar. It reads
head(ws) now.

Same orientation-lie class as the list_head/list_tail sweep, found
independently in two more files by the name census.

two-top/b7c0091:
Two online states offered no way to play at all: the waiting room,
where the summons hangs forever if nobody else is online and the only
exit is CANCEL, and the fled-opponent summary, whose RUN IT BACK slot
went dark (primary_label returned None) leaving just LEAVE. Playing
the bot from either meant knowing to back out to the title, toggle
PRACTICE, and tap PLAY.

Both now offer PLAY THE BOT in the PLAY slot: the waiting room as its
own bordered button (the touch overlays hide while awaiting, so the
band is free), the summary by repurposing the dead primary. The tap
(or P) arms practice, folds the online attempt via leave_online_match
(the same teardown CANCEL and LEAVE run, so nothing new touches the
socket) and bounces through Title for one frame, where PendingBotMatch
re-enters InMatch. The bounce is the point: OnExit despawns and resets
MatchState, the sessionless frame lets the rollback clock zero, and
OnEnter's practice branch builds the bot session. No result is
recorded; the wait staked nothing and a fled opponent's forfeit was
filed when they fled.

A stale pre-flight RUN IT BACK consent no longer renders the
repurposed slot as pressed. No sim change; SIM_VERSION untouched.
perennials/b70e51e:
Pull the full Permapeople database (~9,000 plants, CC BY-SA 4.0) via keyset
pagination and transform the raw dump into app-ready artifacts: a single
fetched dataset plus a facet vocabulary derived from the real data (light,
water, soil, layer, life cycle, growth, edible parts, functions, hardiness,
native range, warnings). Credentials come from the environment; nothing is
committed. Generated data is rebuilt with `npm run data:pull` then
`npm run data:transform`.

Foundation for replacing the hand-authored starter set with real,
source-cited data and a constraint-space search.
bits/b798922:
A puppet's tools live on the puppet now. Tap to select and the halo
appears over it — mouth, eyes, snip, pin, flip, more — with every live
feature drawn as a handle you can take hold of. The mode menu, which
covered 68% of the stage it served, is gone.

The gesture model changes with it:

- A tap selects. It used to move the puppet to the fingertip and record
  a CAST, so choosing a puppet was a destructive act.
- A drag keeps the finger-to-home offset. Without it the puppet jumps
  its centre under the finger on the first move past the threshold.
- The threshold is 6 CSS pixels, not a fraction of the stage: the old
  normalised measure gave nearly twice the slop vertically as
  horizontally on a 9:16 stage.
- A long press is a tap plus a buzz. It selects, keeps the puppet under
  the finger, and opens nothing — a panel under a held finger is fired
  by its own release.
- A tap on bare stage puts the tools away.

Handles are pointer-events: none and the gesture layer hit-tests them
itself, so a pinch's first finger can never be swallowed by a mouth.
The halo goes inert while a pointer is down, so its second finger can
never fire a button. Dragging a handle clear of the puppet takes the
feature off: the banner says so while it is out there, the removal is a
tombstone (the slot stays, so passes driving other pins keep driving
them), and it is undoable for five seconds.

Also in this pass:

- Layering is one REORDER event. It used to re-cast every other puppet,
  so sending one back cost six events and the next drag undid it.
- Hands are assigned from the puppet rather than from a mode with its
  own tap-two-puppets ritual; recording brings the camera up.
- Casts land somewhere free instead of stacking at dead centre, and the
  thing you just cast is selected.
- The stage's pointer layer owns the canvas and nothing else. Every
  overlay inside the frame used to run it too, and the release
  deselected the puppet before the button saw its click.
